answer: At enrollment, an agent proves possession of a key generated and held inside a TEE, while remote attestation verifies the enclave’s MRENCLAVE against approved code. The network binds that key to the identity, so copying a VM image alone cannot reproduce it; creating additional valid identities requires access to genuine TEE hardware, raising the cost of Sybil attacks. Attestation is the bridge between measured code and trust—not a claim that MRENCLAVE is unique per machine. Ivory and lotus are simply example labels, not security properties.
